contentText: Cornell University will ban parties and social events at fraternity houses until the end of the academic year, its president said on Tuesday, responding to the outcry over an alleged ​gang rape on ‌campus in 2024. The measure is the strongest reaction yet from Cornell's leadership to a lawsuit ⁠filed by a former undergraduate, Jane Doe, alleging seven men sexually assaulted her during a party. Over the last several weeks, the Ivy League school in Ithaca, New York, and its ‌president, Michael Kotlikoff, have come under heavy criticism over its response to ⁠the allegations.
